purpose: Add lightweight BFS-based import-graph reachability analysis to security findings, downgrading unreachable code paths from critical/important to minor severity. Implements 20+ entry point patterns across major frameworks and integrates into the existing verifyReviewResult pipeline with graceful fallback.
riskRationale: All iteration 1 code-quality fixes (broken regex, sync I/O, Zod schema gaps, dead code) were correctly applied and the feature architecture is sound. However, a critical import-resolution bug in resolveLocalImport() silently prevents the BFS traversal from following any .js→.ts imports (the project's ESM convention), making the entire analysis a no-op in practice. Zero test coverage on the 321-line module also persists.

text: The PR delivers well-structured reachability analysis with 20+ entry point patterns, clean async I/O, proper Zod schema extensions, and consistent config wiring across all entry points. However, a critical bug in resolveLocalImport() means the BFS traversal cannot resolve .js-extension imports to .ts source files, rendering the entire import-graph analysis non-functional for TypeScript projects using ESM conventions. Combined with zero unit test coverage on the core module, the feature cannot be shipped without these fixes.

reasoning: The critical resolveLocalImport() bug silently breaks all import-graph traversal — the core functionality of this PR. The fix is small and well-defined (see suggestionCode). Auto-fix is appropriate. Once applied and tests are added, this is ready to ship.

message: Comprehensive entry point pattern coverage — 20+ patterns across 7 categories (HTTP frameworks, CLI, WebSocket, message queues, serverless, cron, event emitters) with clear category and label metadata for reporting.

Event emitter regex correctly fixed — the old pattern with consecutive empty char classes would never match real handlers. The new negative lookahead with word boundary on 'data' is precise and correct.
Async I/O migration done properly — all readFileSync/existsSync/statSync calls replaced with fs.promises equivalents for responsive parallel batch processing.
Clean integration into verifyReviewResult with clear separation: reachability enrichment runs first, then meta-verification on enriched results, with graceful fallback on failure.
Zod schema correctly extended with theoreticalRisk and entryPointPath optional fields, preventing silent data stripping at the validation layer when persistence round-trips through JSON.
Configuration propagation is consistent across all three entry points (Action YAML, Action inputs, App env vars) with proper undefined guards.

resolveLocalImport() cannot resolve .js-extension imports to .ts source files — the project's ESM convention (import { foo } from './bar.js'). The function tries exact match (bar.js — doesn't exist), appends extensions (bar.js.ts — doesn't exist), then index files (bar.js/index.ts — doesn't exist). It never strips .js and tries .ts, making the entire BFS import graph traversal a silent no-op.
suggestion: Add a substitution step: if the specifier ends with a known JS extension (.js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs), replace it with the corresponding TS extension before falling through to the index-file check.

message: No unit tests exist for the 321-line reachability module. The BFS traversal, import extraction regex, extension-aware resolution, all 20+ entry point patterns, and batch processing are untested. Existing engine tests set enableReachability: false.
suggestion: Add vitest tests covering: (1) resolveLocalImport with .js→.ts mapping, exact paths, index files; (2) extractImports with ESM, CJS, and dynamic import() patterns; (3) analyzeFindingReachability with mock file trees (reachable vs unreachable); (4) each entry point pattern via content matching; (5) analyzeBatchReachability with mixed results.

message: Dynamic import() calls are not captured by the static import extraction regex, so code-split or lazy-loaded paths are invisible to the BFS traversal. This can cause false positives (marking reachable code as theoretical risk) in Next.js dynamic imports, webpack code splitting, and lazy-loaded route handlers.
suggestion: Add a second regex to match dynamic import() patterns: /import\s*\(\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']\s*\)/g. Collect them alongside static imports in extractImports so they also participate in import graph traversal.

message: Path alias imports (e.g., @/utils/foo, ~/lib/bar) are not resolved by extractImports, which only handles relative imports starting with '.' or '..'. Files reachable only through path aliases will always be flagged as theoretical risk, producing false positives for projects using TypeScript path aliases or webpack resolve aliases.
suggestion: Document this as a known limitation in the module's JSDoc, or optionally add path alias resolution support by reading tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json compilerOptions.paths as a follow-up enhancement.

message: ReachabilityResult.entryPointFile (the actual file path of the entry point) is computed but never propagated to the ReviewIssue — only the human-readable label (entryPointPath) is stored. Downstream consumers cannot identify which file was the nearest entry point.
suggestion: Add entryPointFile to both ReviewIssue and IssueFinding interfaces, then propagate it in the enrichIssues map: entryPointFile: r.entryPointFile alongside entryPointPath.

message: Documentation uses theoretical_risk: true (snake_case) but the actual TypeScript field is theoreticalRisk (camelCase). Line 46 of the same file correctly uses camelCase. This inconsistency could confuse prompt engineers.
suggestion: Change theoretical_risk: true to theoreticalRisk: true on line 5 to match the actual field name and the correct usage on line 46.
